run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T22:41:20Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is driven by error spans in frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' (and 'router frontend egress') operations, whose 5-minute error rate jumped from a pre-burst maximum of 0.0185 spans/s to 0.1074-0.2643 spans/s between 22:33:20 and 22:37:20 and returned to 0.0074 by 22:38:20. The failing request path in that burst is frontend-proxy ingress -> frontend POST /api/checkout -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout's client call oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, which carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 1.3667 spans/s in the 22:34:00 evaluation while other checkout dependencies (cart, currency, product-catalog) show no errors. The only workload rolled out in this window was Deployment payment: its new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 was created at 22:31:42, the old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 was killed at 22:31:45 and the replacement pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d started at 22:31:45. The new ReplicaSet's pod template differs from the old only by the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:31:42Z (same image, env, resources), and the replacement container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 22:33:00.571, which is where the charge failures sit. Hypothesis supported by that evidence: the payment Deployment's pod replacement left no payment gRPC listener for roughly the 22:31:45-22:33:00 interval, so checkout's Charge calls failed and frontend/frontend-proxy returned 5xx. Two further candidates were examined: flagd's paymentUnreachable flag (set to 'on') and the persistent background 503 UC upstream_reset errors on frontend-proxy ingress; neither is established as this alert's cause. Separately, the alert's reported value 0.0222 cannot be reproduced on this target, where frontend-proxy's error-span ratio at 22:41:20 was 0.00056, and no RequestErrorRate alerting rule is loaded on this Prometheus, so the alert's evaluation window/datasource remains unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate was a pre-burst maximum of 0.0185 spans/s for span_name="ingress" across all 5-minute-rate points from 22:11:20 to 22:32:20, then rose to 0.1074 (22:33:20), 0.2556 (22:34:20), 0.2643 (22:35:20), 0.2593 (22:36:20), 0.1519 (22:37:20) and fell to 0.0074 at 22:38:20.

frontend-proxy's second error-bearing operation, span_name="router frontend egress", had STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0 at every 5-minute point from 22:11:20 through 22:32:20, rose to 0.2556 spans/s at 22:34:20-22:36:20, and was 0 again from 22:38:20 onward.

At 60-second resolution, frontend spans 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' all show STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0.9333 spans/s in the 22:33:00 evaluation and 1.3667 spans/s in the 22:34:00 evaluation, and 0 in every other evaluation between 22:25:00 and 22:40:00; checkout spans 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' show STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 1.3667 spans/s only in the 22:34:00 evaluation.

Over 22:33:00-22:40:00 the error-span increases were: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 44.15, checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 44.15, frontend POST 44.15, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 44.15, frontend-proxy ingress 45.23 and frontend-proxy router frontend egress 43.08; all other frontend operations (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/*, tcp.connect) were 0 in that window.

Only the checkout Charge call failed among checkout's dependencies in the burst window: at 22:34:20-22:38:20 the ERROR-status series returned were checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge plus frontend POST/POST /api/checkout/executing api route (pages) /api/checkout/grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and frontend-proxy ingress/router frontend egress; checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and HTTP POST carried no error status.

The payment service's own error ratio was 0 at every 2-minute point from 22:12:20 to 22:50:20, while the same query returned 0.0253/0.0250 for frontend-proxy at 22:34:20/22:36:20, 0.0560/0.0438 for checkout at 22:34:20/22:36:20 and 0.0235/0.0238 for frontend at 22:34:20/22:36:20.

payment's server-side span_name="grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" rate was 1.4333 spans/s at 22:31:45 and 22:32:00, 0.2 at 22:32:45 and 22:33:00, 0 at every 15-second evaluation from 22:33:15 to 22:36:30, then 1.4333 at 22:36:45 and 22:37:00; payment's span status was STATUS_CODE_UNSET throughout with no ERROR samples for its charge spans.

Deployment payment in otel-demo was rolled at 22:31:42-22:31:45: Deployment payment ScalingReplicaSet scaled up payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1 at 22:31:42 and scaled down payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0 at 22:31:45; ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 SuccessfulCreate at 22:31:42; Pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 Killing at 22:31:45; Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled 22:31:42, Created 22:31:44, Started 22:31:45.

The new payment ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 (created 22:31:42) and the old payment-55766d76b9 (created 21:59:30) have identical containers (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, identical env incl. PAYMENT_PORT=8080 and FLAGD_HOST=flagd, identical cpu/memory limits and securityContext, no volumes); their pod templates differ only by the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:31:42Z present on the new one.

The only payment log line in 22:31:40-22:33:30 is 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 22:33:00.571, and charge lines ('Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.') are present again from 22:36:19.487 onward.

Across the otel-demo Deployments only payment carries deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2 with a status condition update at 22:31:45Z (flagd is revision 2 with condition update 22:01:27Z; every other of the 21 Deployments is revision 1), and all 21 Deployments report 1 available/1 ready replica.
Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d is Running with container restartCount 0 and a single container 'payment'; no pod in otel-demo shows a last termination reason or non-zero restart count.
The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo currently sets flag paymentUnreachable to defaultVariant "on" (description 'Payment service is unavailable') and paymentFailure to defaultVariant "off".

After the burst, frontend-proxy error spans continue at background level: increase over 22:40:00-22:57:49 is 8.41 for span_name="ingress" and 0 for span_name="router frontend egress", and 39.07 ingress error spans accrued over 21:41:20-22:33:00.

frontend-proxy's remaining ingress 5xx are logged as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/cart, /api/data/?contextKeys=... and /api/products/... at 22:40:02, 22:40:35, 22:40:49, 22:43:33 and 22:44:36, i.e. the upstream frontend terminated the connection rather than returning an application error.
On this target, frontend-proxy's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span ratio at 22:41:20 (5-minute window) evaluates to 0.0005596, not the 0.0222 reported in the alert annotation.

This Prometheus exposes only traces_span_metrics_calls_total/traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for request telemetry plus infrastructure/container metrics; no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count or app_payment_transactions_total series exist in the queried window (the broad metric-name query returned 63 names, none of those).

The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is caused by Deployment otel-demo/payment: its pod replacement at 22:31:42-22:31:45 (kubectl restartedAt-only template change) killed the only payment pod, the replacement's gRPC server only began listening at 22:33:00.571, and during that gap checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls returned STATUS_CODE_ERROR (1.3667 spans/s in the 22:34:00 minute), which propagated as checkout PlaceOrder errors, frontend POST /api/checkout errors and frontend-proxy ingress/egress error spans.

A second candidate is the flagd flag paymentUnreachable="on" in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, whose declared fault ('Payment service is unavailable') matches the observed payment-unreachable failure path; it cannot be confirmed or excluded for 22:31 because the flag's value at that time is unknown.

The paymentUnreachable flag cannot be shown to drive these charge failures: while the ConfigMap still shows it 'on', checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge error rate is 0 from 22:34:30 onward and payment serves charges again (grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 1.4333 spans/s at 22:36:45-22:37:00 and 0.9-1.5 spans/s thereafter) with 0 error ratio for the payment service; the observed failure was confined to roughly one minute and time-locked to the pod replacement rather than to a sustained flag state.

The flagd Deployment revision-2 rollout at 22:01:27 is not supported as the trigger of this alert: it precedes the error deviation by about 30 minutes, frontend-proxy's 5-minute ingress error rate stayed at 0-0.0185 spans/s through 22:32:20, and the only error burst begins after the 22:31:42-22:31:45 payment pod replacement.

Because frontend-proxy's ingress error rate never reaches zero (39.07 error spans over 21:41:20-22:33:00 and 8.41 over 22:40:00-22:57:49, all background 503 'upstream_reset_before_response_started' from frontend), an alert thresholded strictly 'above 0' can remain firing after the burst ends; the rule expression that would confirm this is not available on this target.

Retrieve audit/change history for otel-demo Deployment payment at 2026-11-16T22:31:42Z (the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation shows a rollout restart) to identify who or what issued it, and check the flagd-config ConfigMap history around the same time to establish whether paymentUnreachable was toggled.

Review the payment Deployment's startup and shutdown behavior (the replacement container needed ~75 s from container start to 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080', and the old pod was killed at 22:31:45) so that readiness gating and graceful shutdown avoid a window with no charge listener during rollouts.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not available on this target: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data (evidence 3310ad34-ffeb-43ac-a184-13abb76488fa-t0:6a8720bb-089e-48dd-b450-453507c1e246) and a type=alert listing returned no rules (dfd93da0-e4ba-4dca-a850-b46fd9508b27-t0:30ac4afa-ab61-45fa-8302-ca6ea44d921c), so the rule expression, evaluation window and datasource behind the reported value 0.0222 are unknown; the value cannot be reproduced here (0.0005596 at 22:41:20), and a 1-minute ingress-ratio evaluation at 22:41:20 returned no data (0a61bb7a-ffa4-4cdc-836d-04aab4b8df76-t1:9cdcf7a2-ffca-4a34-8d54-240ba87612a0).

No span-level error details are available: traces_search returned no traces for frontend-proxy in 22:30:00-22:45:00 and 22:45:00-22:57:49, for checkout in 22:30:00-22:40:00, and for frontend in 22:50:00-22:57:49 (e.g. 61fe369c-314e-4db4-a7de-f5a3d8265bd9-t0:634e7b63-a473-4211-96ab-6b8af76f5ac1, c46e6e5f-d9ed-490b-ae4b-3798653f0c3b-t1:618c7241-79b9-4c01-adb5-f25f2bc3ef7a), so the exact gRPC status/message of the failed Charge calls is unknown.

Pod logs are only available up to about 22:45:40-22:45:43 for the otel-demo pods read (frontend-proxy, payment, checkout), so log evidence for the rest of the window, including any further 503s after 22:45, is unknown.

The deleted old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 no longer exists, so its shutdown behaviour and any errors it logged after 22:31:45 cannot be read; the frontend container also returned no log lines in 22:25:00-22:50:00.

What or who triggered the payment rollout restart at 22:31:42 is unknown: change_history is not an integrated data source in this Run, the pod template change is only the restartedAt annotation, and no audit evidence is available; secrets could not be read and were not needed.

The flagd flag state at incident time is unknown: the ConfigMap read is the object's current state (paymentUnreachable="on"), and there is no change history for it, so whether the flag changed around 22:31 cannot be verified.

payment's exported span series for grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge are absent from 22:33:15 to 22:36:30 while its logs show charge handling resuming at about 22:33, so the trace-metric coverage for payment during the gap is incomplete and the exact duration of payment unavailability is uncertain.

No error-span series was returned for cart, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote, shipping or load-generator in the queried window, so their health was not verified and they are neither confirmed healthy nor affected. accounting, payment, ad, fraud-detection and recommendation were checked: accounting and payment showed 0 error ratio, ad/fraud-detection/recommendation only their steady flagd EventStream rate (~0.0037 spans/s, unchanged before and after), which is background.

No pre-incident baseline older than ~22:11 is available (the otel-demo pods were created at 21:59:29-22:01:24 and a frontend-proxy error-rate query for 20:00:00-21:41:00 returned no data), so a longer trend for the ingress error rate cannot be assessed.
next_steps: Query the alert-evaluating system (not this target) for the RequestErrorRate rule definition for service frontend-proxy to confirm its PromQL expression, window and evaluation delay, and why 0.022222 was reported at 2026-11-16T22:41:20Z.

Obtain audit/change history for the payment Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-16T22:31:42Z and for ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config around that time to identify the actor and whether paymentUnreachable was modified.

If this alert is meant to catch real user-facing errors, consider requiring an error-ratio magnitude well above the recurring background 503 'upstream_reset_before_response_started' level rather than a strict 'above 0' threshold.
Inspect the frontend (Node.js) upstream connection-reset behavior that produces the recurring ingress 503s, since those keep frontend-proxy's ingress error spans non-zero between incidents.
